items.content:
I’ve seen a lot of complaints about “AI slop” on LinkedIn. 

The problem isn’t AI, it’s how you’re using it. 

Look, we all use AI. 
If you don’t…you should. 

But you always need to add that human touch. 

You know when someone hasn’t: 

→ Overly perfect grammar 
→ Paragraphs starting with "Furthermore"
→ Words like "leverage, "foster" and "synergy"
→ Generic takes that could have been written by anyone

You need to add your voice. 

Here's how to make sure your content sounds like you:

Step 1: Read everything out loud before you publish
↳ If it doesn't sound like something you'd actually say…
↳ Rewrite it. Remove any words that feel unnatural 

Step 2: Find your own vocabulary
↳ The words you use when you're excited or annoyed
↳ Write down 10 to 15 phrases you use in real conversation
↳ Add those words to your LinkedIn posts 

Step 3: Build a voice bank
↳ Record yourself talking about your content ideas
↳ Ask AI (or me) to convert that into a post 
↳ Include the phrases you repeat 

Step 4: Write like you text 
↳ Include abbreviations you use in text
↳ Include emojis that you’d add to texts 
↳ Keep it short, simple and concise 

Step 5: Never publish the first draft
↳ The first draft is what AI gives you
↳ The second draft is where your voice comes back
↳ Edit until it sounds like you then publish

AI is not there to replace your voice. 

It’s there to amplify it.

STOP POSTING AND GHOSTING!!!

If you want to grow → you need to comment. 

Posting alone is not enough...

1 post = 1 opportunity to be seen
10 comments = 10 more opportunities to be seen. 

Use the STANLEY Comment Method:

S - Skip generic responses

❌ Generic: "Great post!"
✅ Good: "This is exactly what I discovered when writing 50 LinkedIn posts last month."

T - Target with questions
✅ Ask questions to continue conversation 
🎯 Formula: [Acknowledge point] + [Add insight] + [Ask specific question]

A - Add your perspective
✅ Don't be shy...tell them how you really feel 
🎯 Template: "Love this angle. In my experience [specific example]. One thing I'd add: [insight]."

N - Narrate mini-stories
✅ Add your own experience 
🎯 Template: "This reminds me of last week when...

L - Lead with respect (even disagreeing)
✅ Speak to others as you'd like to spoken to 
🎯 Template: "I see this differently. I get [their view],  but I've found [alternative] works better because..."

E - Engage authentically
✅ Show off your personality 
🎯 Your comment = mini-post

Y - Your next move
✅ Set a timer for 10 minutes.
✅ Write 5 thoughtful comments.

Do this every day and watch your profile views triple.

Bonus: Comments create validated post ideas.

If a comment gets good reach and engagement?
It will make a great post.

Your comments are content too.

Treat them that way.

items.content:
I analyzed 98,611 LinkedIn posts (I’ve helped write).  

The top performers have this in common: 

1. They use a visual

🌠 Image posts outperform text-only by 1.6x
🌠 Carousels and text get shared more
🌠 Polls and articles are bottom of the list

2. Write longer posts

✍️ The sweet spot is 1,200 to 1,800 characters
✍️ 2.7x the engagement of posts under 200 chars
✍️ Longer posts earn longer dwell time

3. Format for scanning

✅ 41+ line breaks vs 1-5 line breaks = 5x gap in engagement
✅ White space is not wasted space
✅ One idea per line

4. Keep the hook short

🪝 Your hook should fit on one line
🪝 Under 60 characters outperforms by 2x
🪝 First line hooks, second line rehooks

5. Ask questions

❓ End every post with a question
❓ Make it easy to answer in one or two words
❓ 4+ questions pull 60% more comments than posts with 0

6. Drop the hashtags
# No hashtags vs 7+ hashtags = 39% higher engagement
# Hashtags do not increase your reach
# They make your post look spammy

7. Never put links in the post

🔗 The algo punishes you for sending people away
🔗 One link in the post = 43% engagement drop
🔗 Always put the link in the first comment

8. Time it right

🕐 Engagement drops 1.6x by 10pm
🕐 Weekday mornings peak at 6 to 7am local time
🕐 Weekends run 17% below the weekday median

The biggest finding:

Nail all eight fundamentals and you get 8x the engagement of someone who nails none.

They stack.

Every habit adds up.

items.content:
Most people post one type of content on LinkedIn. 

(That’s exactly why they stay stuck).

Every post you write should do one of three jobs: 

 1. Posts that grow your audience

🎯 These are for people who don’t know you exist yet. 
🎯 They might not be problem-aware yet. 
🎯 These need to stop them scrolling. 

Do this: 

→ Talk about their problems using language they use 
→ Challenge something they’ve assumed was true 
→ Lean on emotions they’ve felt before 

2. Posts that build your credibility

🎯 These are for people who know you
🎯 But they don't trust you just yet 
🎯 These posts need to show you’re worth listening to. 

Do this: 

→ Solve a problem they suffer with daily 
→ Make your advice so easy they can apply it today 
→ Keep the solution not complex to look smart

3. Posts that fill your pipeline

🎯 These are for people ready to buy but need a push
🎯 Your job is to create FOMO so they act now. 

Do this: 

→ Show what happens when people work with you
→ Use your results to show you can make impact 
→ Focus on the transformation of working with you 

The weekly mix that works:
✅ 2x grow your audience: broad, relatable, easy to share
✅ 2x build credibility: specific, educational, saveable
✅ 1x fill your pipeline: proof, results, direct CTA

All three style of posts work together. 

If you just do one, it won’t work at all. 


Which type are you skipping right now?

I’ve helped grow 3,885 LinkedIn accounts.

If you want to hit 10K followers this is the roadmap: 

🚀 0 to 500: Prove you exist
→ Pick one outcome (growth, clients, authority)
→ Choose 2-4 content pillars & stick to them
→ Comment on 10 posts every day 
→ Post 3 x per week minimum 
→ Write as you talk

🎯 Your only goal here is not quitting.

🚀 500 to 2K: Get specific.
→ Name your audience (title, industry, problems)
→ Study your top performing posts & do more of that
→ Reply to every comment within 60 minutes of posting
→ Share what's working and what failed

🎯 People trust progress, not perfection.

🚀 2K to 5K: Build the engine
→ One story-driven post per week
→ Save every high-performing post
→ Comment like it's content
→ Track saves and DMs

🎯 If your DMs are quiet, your content isn't converting.

🚀 5K to 10K: Repurpose and convert
→ Turn your top 5 posts into carousels and infographics
→ One conversion post per week (results & proof)
→ Collaborate with creators at your level
→ Earn trust through your content 

🎯 At this stage, consistency is the product.

Knowing what to post on LinkedIn can seem complicated. 

But the content system behind it is simple: 

There are 4 buckets you need to choose from…

1. Your story

→ Share what happened 
→ What worked and what didn't
→ The moment everything changed
→ What you'd do differently next time 

💜 People love following journeys 

2. Your client's world

→ Describe their problem better than they can
→ The frustration they can't articulate
→ What they stress about late at night 
→ The outcome they actually want

💜 When someone reads your post and thinks "that's me" you've won

3. Your industry

→ Say the things others are too polite to say
→ The advice everyone gives that doesn't work
→ Why the conventional wisdom is wrong
→ What's broken in your space

💜 Conviction builds authority faster than expertise

4. Your skills

→ Teach others how to do what you do
→ Show what you know in a way that's useful
→ Show your clients why they need you to do it
→ Frameworks, processes, and systems that worked

💜 Teaching builds more trust than telling

Don't know what to write…

Use this structure:

→ Here's the problem your reader has
→ Here's why it's costing them
→ Here's what they actually want instead
→ Here's what to do about it
→ Here's what changes when they do
→ Here's the line that makes them act

Before you publish run it through this checklist:

✅ Does it use language your clients actually use?
✅ Is the main point something they can act on today?
✅ Does it come from a real story or real experience?
✅ Is it simple enough to understand in one read?
✅ Does it describe their pain and their desired outcome?
✅ Would you be proud of it in six months?

Score it out of six → if it gets four or more, publish it.

Perfectionism kills more content than bad writing ever will.

I've helped write 40,451 LinkedIn posts.

This is the viral framework you need to use: 

(Use this and your account will grow) 

It's called the S.T.A.N.L.E.Y. method:

S — Spot what people care about
↳ What's your ideal customer annoyed about?
↳ What's a problem they’re facing right now?
↳ That’s what your post should be about

T — Turn it into a hook
↳ Turn that problem into a short, punchy line
↳ Try to keep it to 10 words max
↳ Open a loop to intrigue people

A — Add your experience
↳ Include social proof to establish authority
↳ Share what you’ve seen or tried yourself
↳ People don’t want theories they want proof

N — Name your steps
↳ Give people something to follow
↳ Lists and frameworks always land
↳ Make your post feel useful immediately

L — Leave them with something memorable
↳ Each post should have one lesson
↳ End needs to be as strong as the beginning
↳ Leave your reader feeling inspired

E — Engage your audience
↳ Ask one simple question
↳ This is your call-to-engage
↳ Make them want to hit comment

Y — Your next step
↳ Tell the reader exactly what to do next
↳ This is your call-to-action
↳ Ask them to comment, follow or share
